title: Installation and version management
expected: Prints the actual executable and pinned runtime. A different version fails explicitly.

title: CLI and REPL
expected: eval has no result output; print writes 5; main prints a greeting; the intentionally invalid fixture fails parsing.

title: Minimal project structure
expected: The application prints 5 and its addition test passes.

title: Environment configuration
expected: Valid configuration prints public fields. Invalid ports fail without exposing the fixture secret.

title: Command-line arguments and output contracts
expected: Valid input is JSON on stdout; an invalid flag produces stderr and a nonzero exit.

title: Interactive terminal input
expected: --yes confirms; piped input is deliberately rejected instead of hanging for a TTY.

title: Application watch mode
expected: Edit message.mjs in another editor: watch mode restarts and prints the changed message. Stop with Ctrl+C.

title: Scope and closures
expected: Independent counters produce [1,2,1]; var closures see 3,3,3 and let closures see 0,1,2.

title: Objects, destructuring, and mutation
expected: Nullish defaults preserve port 0; copied nested state still shares identity unless copied explicitly.

title: Classes, prototypes, and this
expected: An unbound method fails; binding or calling through its receiver produces 1 then 2.

title: Collections and identity
expected: Set removes repeated primitives; distinct objects remain distinct; WeakMap stores non-enumerable object metadata.

title: Iterators and generators
expected: Only ten values are produced; breaking the loop executes generator cleanup.

title: Serialization and numeric boundaries
expected: A decimal string preserves an integer beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; dates need explicit reconstruction.

title: Unicode and regular expressions
expected: Normalization equates canonical text; the emoji occupies 2 UTF-16 units, 1 code point, and 4 UTF-8 bytes.

title: Dates, locales, and time zones
expected: Madrid jumps from 01:30 to 03:30. Currency formatting depends on locale/ICU; it does not convert currency.

title: Blocking versus nonblocking execution
expected: Concurrent I/O waits overlap; synchronous CPU work serializes the server. Printed durations are measurements, not fixed timing promises.

title: Event-loop phases
expected: Inside the I/O callback immediate precedes timeout. Top-level timeout/immediate order is deliberately not asserted.

title: Microtasks and next-tick callbacks
expected: CJS prints sync,nextTick,promise,microtask; ESM prints sync,promise,microtask,nextTick for this top-level fixture.

title: The libuv worker pool
expected: Each fresh process measures eight crypto jobs sharing libuv resources; more threads are not guaranteed to improve elapsed time.

title: Timers and cancellation
expected: AbortError is observed; manually owned timers are cleared.

title: Resource lifetime and process exit
expected: Active timer/server resources appear before cleanup; the process then exits naturally. Resource names vary by platform.

title: Callback conventions and promisification
expected: The callback adapter yields 6, and an error-first rejection is handled.

title: Promise aggregation
expected: all rejects, allSettled retains three outcomes, any returns A, and all-rejected any raises AggregateError.

title: Sequential and concurrent await
expected: Both workflows produce 5; independent waits overlap in the concurrent version. Timings are measured.

title: Bounded concurrency
expected: Twenty tasks preserve result order with at most three active; one failure does not stop the remaining work.

title: Cancellation and deadlines
expected: The timers promise rejects AbortError; the combined signal records TimeoutError as its deadline reason.

title: Error propagation and cleanup
expected: Cleanup runs before the caller observes the wrapped error and its original cause.

title: Async generators
expected: Only the first page is requested; breaking async iteration runs cleanup.

title: ES modules
expected: ESM imports with explicit extensions work; Node rejects the extensionless fixture.

title: CommonJS
expected: Resolved CommonJS module instances are cached; the two calls share the same counter.

title: ESM–CommonJS interoperability
expected: Both interop paths return 42; require rejects an ESM graph containing top-level await.

title: Package exports and imports
expected: A real tarball installs into a separate consumer: public import returns 42 and private subpath import fails.

title: Dynamic imports and plugins
expected: The allowlisted plugin runs; arbitrary path input is rejected.

title: Module-relative assets and JSON imports
expected: Module-relative assets load consistently even when the shell current directory changes.

title: Circular dependencies
expected: An eagerly evaluated cycle fails; extracting shared state removes the cycle.

title: Package metadata and dependency types
expected: The manifest separates dependency responsibilities and the optional feature has an actual fallback.

title: Portable npm scripts
expected: A portable Node cleanup removes only a generated, project-owned directory.

title: Lockfiles and reproducible installation
expected: Offline local dependency installation creates a real lockfile; ci succeeds, then rejects manifest drift.

title: Semantic versioning and updates
expected: Real semver evaluation demonstrates exact, caret, tilde, and pre-1.0 ranges.

title: npm workspaces
expected: Two real local workspaces link without workspace:* syntax; the CLI imports the math package.

title: Dependency inspection and security review
expected: The actual installed graph is inspected. --audit optionally requests live advisories; no fabricated vulnerability counts or force-fixes.

title: Packaging and publishing preparation
expected: The npm pack dry run includes the distributable entry and excludes the secret-shaped fixture. No package is published.

title: Filesystem operations
expected: The temporary file is created, appended, read through an owned handle, and removed.

title: Paths and containment
expected: Existing-file resolution permits the fixture and rejects traversal, absolute input and missing files.

title: Directory traversal
expected: A lazy recursive walker finds two real fixtures and avoids following symbolic links.

title: Safe file replacement
expected: Injected failure preserves old content and removes the partial file; success publishes new content.

title: File permissions and exclusive creation
expected: Exclusive creation rejects an overwrite. Mode 0600 has POSIX semantics; Windows privacy requires ACL consideration.

title: Buffers and binary layouts
expected: A versioned big-endian binary packet round-trips; malformed/truncated frames are rejected.

title: Text encodings and chunk boundaries
expected: Every possible two-chunk split preserves the Unicode text; incomplete bytes are buffered until decoder end.

title: File watching
expected: Reconciliation serializes scans and reaches the real directory state despite coalesced watcher hints.

title: EventEmitter lifecycle
expected: The once listener fires once and the owned progress listener is removed.

title: Asynchronous event listeners
expected: emit returns immediately; the rejected async listener reaches the configured synchronous error observer.

title: Readable and writable backpressure
expected: The slow sink receives every chunk exactly once while the producer honors drain. highWaterMark is a threshold, not a universal memory cap.

title: Transform streams
expected: Byte-by-byte input preserves UTF-8, filters records, and flushes the final line without a newline.

title: Pipelines and failure cleanup
expected: Pipeline failure destroys participants and removes partial output; an incomplete result is never published.

title: Async iteration over streams
expected: Early async-iterator break destroys the source and releases its file handle.

title: Web Streams interoperability
expected: A real local fetch Web ReadableStream is adapted into a Node pipeline and published only after success.

title: Streaming compression
expected: Both codecs round-trip actual bytes and reject an output budget smaller than the fixture. Sizes are measured.

title: URLs and query parameters
expected: Repeated query values, percent encoding and relative resolution are shown without making a network request.

title: Core HTTP server
expected: The real HTTP API is exercised through success, missing route, malformed JSON and body-limit cases.

title: HTTP clients and connection reuse
expected: The first connection is new; subsequent reuse is measured, not assumed. The owned Agent is destroyed.

title: Fetch, cancellation, and HTTP errors
expected: A local fault server demonstrates HTTP status errors, invalid JSON and cancellation without relying on the public internet.

title: HTTPS and TLS verification
expected: The complete local CA/certificate lab verifies trust and hostname checks; TLS verification is never disabled.

title: HTTP/2 multiplexing
expected: Two HTTP/2 streams share a session; cancelling one does not cancel the other. Cleartext is for this loopback lab only.

title: TCP framing
expected: Every split point and a real fragmented TCP exchange produce two complete application frames.

title: UDP datagrams
expected: The receiver logs actual datagrams and computes missing sequence 4 at the application layer. UDP itself does not promise delivery/order.

title: DNS and address selection
expected: The OS resolver reads localhost configuration. Optional --network queries real A/AAAA records without inventing addresses.

title: Process lifecycle and signals
expected: A finite harness calls idempotent shutdown twice but cleans up only once.

title: Child processes without shell interpolation
expected: Shell-looking input is printed literally by a child process using an argument array, never interpolated.

title: Interprocess communication
expected: Request IDs correlate replies; a missing reply times out and removes its pending entry.

title: Worker threads
expected: The worker computes 5000050000 on its own JavaScript thread and exits naturally.

title: Worker pools
expected: A bounded two-thread pool computes a result and rejects excess queued work.

title: Message channels and transferable data
expected: Transfer detaches the sender ArrayBuffer while the receiver owns the original-sized storage.

title: Shared memory and Atomics
expected: Two workers update one shared counter without a read-modify-write race.

title: Clustered processes
expected: Two separate processes serve a shared listening endpoint. Observed PID distribution is not required to alternate. Shutdown prevents respawn loops.

title: Framework routing and lifecycle
expected: Fastify lifecycle hooks run; thrown async errors become sanitized 500 responses. Add --serve to inspect endpoints manually.

title: Express middleware
expected: Express 5 forwards rejected route promises to the four-argument error middleware; unknown routes remain 404.

title: Request and response validation
expected: Invalid input yields 400, while the response schema strips an internal field from the successful 201 response.

title: REST pagination and filtering
expected: Cursor traversal returns each fixture ID exactly once and rejects unbounded limits.

title: OpenAPI contracts
expected: The generated OpenAPI document contains the real route and agrees with its response contract.

title: Streaming file uploads
expected: A real multipart client uploads a small file; an oversized stream yields 413 and removes its partial output.

title: WebSocket communication
expected: A native WebSocket client exchanges validated JSON with the external ws server; heartbeat and listener resources are cleaned up.

title: Server-sent events
expected: Reconnection replays only events after Last-Event-ID; disconnect clears heartbeat state.

title: Browser integration and CORS
expected: The API emits its configured allow-origin value. A browser on a different origin cannot read the response even though the HTTP request can succeed.

title: Embedded SQLite — experimental
expected: Reopening the real SQLite file preserves the first record; each execution inserts another record. Database operations remain synchronous.

title: PostgreSQL and connection pooling
expected: The parameterized attack-shaped title is stored as ordinary data and the table remains intact.

title: Transactions
expected: Failure between updates rolls back both balances; success preserves the total with deterministic lock ordering.

title: Schema migrations
expected: A migration is applied transactionally and its default preserves compatibility. A complete node-pg-migrate file is also supplied.

title: Concurrent updates
expected: Two concurrent updates using the same expected version produce one success and one conflict.

title: MongoDB document modeling
expected: A unique SKU index supports an idempotent upsert; a duplicate insert is rejected and the real query plan is displayed.

title: Redis caching
expected: Miss loads DB, hit avoids it, commit-plus-invalidation refreshes it, and a closed cache falls back to PostgreSQL.

title: Pub/Sub versus durable streams
expected: Pub/Sub delivers only to a live subscriber; the retained stream is read through a consumer group and acknowledged.

title: Durable background jobs
expected: The worker fails twice and succeeds within a three-attempt retry budget; job resources are closed.

title: Scheduling and overlap policies
expected: The real scheduler records an explicit timezone; immediate jobs verify the global concurrency bound. Tomorrow’s scheduled execution is not claimed.

title: Transactional outbox
expected: Two deliveries produce one durable business effect, protected by a PostgreSQL uniqueness constraint and transaction.

title: Secrets and configuration hygiene
expected: A mounted-file fixture configures the app; missing configuration fails generically and never prints the secret.

title: Password derivation
expected: Versioned, salted scrypt records verify correctly without logging passwords or hashes.

title: Cookie sessions and CSRF
expected: Real session and CSRF plugins reject the missing token and accept the matching one. Tokens and keys are not printed.

title: JWT verification
expected: Signature and claim validation accepts only the expected issuer/audience/algorithm and a live expiry. No tokens are logged.

title: Resource authorization
expected: Real signed identities and PostgreSQL owner predicates prevent cross-user access.

title: Webhook signatures and replay prevention
expected: Raw-byte signature verification precedes parsing; a database transaction combines durable deduplication and the business update.

title: Authenticated encryption
expected: Authenticated encryption round-trips hello and rejects a modified ciphertext. Nonces must be unique per key.

title: Outbound-request restrictions
expected: A server-owned destination map, redirect rejection and body cap are tested against a real loopback fixture.

title: Abuse and resource controls
expected: The actual rate-limit plugin enforces 20 requests per window and the body cap rejects a separate oversized request.

title: Runtime permissions
expected: Granted read/write work; a read outside the grant fails. The permission model is not a malicious-code sandbox.

title: Unit tests
expected: Boundary tests check valid ports and reject malformed/unsafe input.

title: Asynchronous tests and teardown
expected: A real HTTP fixture uses an OS-assigned port; test cleanup closes it even when assertions fail.

title: Integration tests
expected: A real Fastify request persists a row that is verified through a separate SQL query; an isolated schema is removed afterward.

title: Mocks and deterministic time
expected: Mock time advances exactly to a deadline without real sleeping; timer mocks restore after the test.

title: Property-based testing
expected: Generated byte arrays round-trip through the actual codec; the seed makes failures reproducible.

title: Coverage — experimental
expected: The real coverage report changes when a negative-total branch is tested. No coverage percentage is fabricated.

title: Linting and formatting
expected: ESLint finds actual unused/undefined identifiers; Prettier distinguishes unformatted and formatted source.

title: Interactive debugging
expected: The regression test fails on -1900 from the buggy formula and passes on 80 after the fix.

title: Stack traces and source maps
expected: The generated bundle fails in both runs; source maps point the second stack back to the original source.

title: Structured logging
expected: Real JSON logs preserve the correlation ID and structured error while removing configured sensitive fields.

title: Asynchronous request context
expected: Overlapping requests retain their own IDs and the outer context remains undefined.

title: Diagnostics channels
expected: Diagnostics are emitted synchronously only while subscribed; business results remain 6 and 8.

title: Runtime measurements
expected: Actual duration, utilization and delay reveal blocking work. Delay nanoseconds are converted to milliseconds.

title: Application metrics
expected: Actual Prometheus text includes bounded success/error labels, histogram samples and an in-flight gauge that returns to zero.

title: Distributed tracing
expected: Two actual Node processes propagate W3C trace context through HTTP. Trace IDs and parent-child relationships are asserted.

title: CPU profiling
expected: A real CPU profile is generated under this lesson’s profiles directory and can be opened in DevTools.

title: Memory leaks and heap analysis
expected: The unbounded cache retains 80000 entries while the bounded cache retains 1000; heap usage is measured rather than assumed.

title: Load testing and bottlenecks
expected: Actual HTTP timings and EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans are measured before and after an index. The lab does not assume the index always wins.

title: Resource budgets
expected: Exactly eight slots run concurrently, 32 wait, and the next submission is rejected. All accepted work drains.

title: Retry budgets and backoff
expected: Transient failures consume three of four attempts; permanent errors do not retry; a pre-aborted caller starts no work.

title: Circuit breakers and recovery
expected: Three failures open the breaker; an open call never reaches the dependency, and a later successful probe closes it.

title: Graceful shutdown
expected: A real HTTP request drains before a real SQLite connection closes; shutdown is idempotent.

title: Native TypeScript execution
expected: Native execution strips erasable types and prints 42 despite a static type error; the TypeScript checker rejects it.

title: TypeScript compilation and declarations
expected: Compilation emits runnable JavaScript, declarations and source maps; the compiled library returns the greeting.

title: Type checking JavaScript with JSDoc
expected: JavaScript permits string concatenation at runtime; JSDoc checking detects the bad argument and accepts the fixed call.

title: Native addons with Node-API
expected: After native compilation, the addon returns 42 and rejects a nonnumeric argument.

title: WebAssembly
expected: Compiled WAT executes as WebAssembly; i32 overflow wraps rather than producing the same Number result as unbounded JS.

title: Module compile caching
expected: Cache status and full-process startup times are measured. Caching does not cache exported business results or guarantee a speedup.

title: Trusted code in VM contexts
expected: Trusted code uses separate global state and the synchronous infinite-loop fixture times out. vm is not a security boundary.

title: Deprecated API migration
expected: The actual runtime reports legacy warnings or removal errors; modern code preserves the content without relying on deprecated APIs.

title: Container packaging
expected: The complete two-stage Docker image builds, serves a real request as USER node, and the owned container stops.

title: Continuous integration
expected: The supplied multi-OS GitHub Actions workflow runs reproducible installation and the real validation commands.

title: Deployment configuration
expected: The Compose stack builds, writes a task, replaces only api1, and verifies the task survives in PostgreSQL.

title: Health checks
expected: Readiness changes independently of liveness. Dependency failure is injected at the pool boundary, not falsely reported as a physical database outage.

title: Horizontal scaling
expected: Two actual app instances with independent pools and a shared signing key read the same PostgreSQL task.

title: Deployment and rollback
expected: Mixed versions read the old authoritative field. After old writers drain, a catch-up backfill repairs even non-null stale derived values.

title: Backup, restore, and maintenance
expected: A real custom-format PostgreSQL archive restores into a fresh, separately named database and its fixture is checked before cleanup.

title: Serverless runtime compatibility
expected: Actual Node invocations demonstrate warm module state versus a fresh process. The supplied SAM template can be invoked locally with SAM CLI and Docker.

title: Single executable applications — experimental 1.1
expected: The actual single executable builds and runs with PATH emptied, demonstrating that the Node runtime is embedded.

title: WASI — experimental
expected: A real WASI program opens hello.txt through its preopened directory and prints Hello from WASI.

title: Module customization hooks — experimental 1.2
expected: The preload hook resolves only explicit aliases, preserves node: imports and rejects an unknown alias.

title: Foreign function interface — experimental, Node.js 26.1+
expected: After building the supplied native C library for this OS/architecture, FFI returns 42 and closes its handle.

title: Virtual filesystem — experimental, Node.js 26.4+
expected: Mounted reads succeed, cleanup unmounts the fixture, and irreversible read-only mode rejects writes. VFS is not a sandbox.

title: Built-in benchmark runner — experimental 1.0, Node.js 26.9+
expected: The actual experimental benchmark runner measures two equivalent string operations. Results depend on runtime and hardware.

title: Iterable Streams API — experimental
expected: Both actual stream interfaces produce uppercase output. The experimental iterable API and stable classic pipeline remain distinct.

title: Command-Line File-Processing Tool
expected: The complete streaming CLI filters records, counts malformed data, handles a final line without newline, and atomically preserves an existing output on failure.

title: Database-Backed API with Authentication
expected: A complete task API registers/logs in real users, enforces ownership, rejects stale edits and rolls back an injected batch failure.

title: Real-Time Collaboration Application
expected: Three actual clients communicate across two server instances; an offline client replays a missed event from PostgreSQL and an unauthorized upgrade is rejected.

title: Background-Job Processing System
expected: A separate worker process really exits after publishing its result but before ACK. Recovery retries the stalled job and the database proves one durable effect.

title: Deployed Application with Monitoring and Graceful Shutdown
expected: The real Compose deployment serves two API replicas behind NGINX, completes a BullMQ report, exposes metrics and survives API replacement.
